terms.definition: The total length of the path an object actually travels.
terms.function: Counts every meter of real path — curves, detours, and right turns included.
terms.whereItIs: A scalar readout that grows with the hiker along the course.
terms.whyItMatters: It's the base number used in speed = distance ÷ time and the honest measure of how much ground was truly covered.

terms.definition: A quantity that has size but no direction.
terms.whyItMatters: Because distance is a scalar, it can never be negative and never decreases as motion continues.
terms.whereItIs: The counter that only climbs — no arrow is attached to it.

terms.definition: The straight-line vector from a start point to a stop point.
terms.whyItMatters: It's the shortcut a crow would fly, usually far shorter than the full winding distance, and it can be zero after a round trip.
terms.whereItIs: The dashed straight arrow drawn beside the winding path.

terms.definition: The actual route an object takes — every bend and detour its meters are counted along.
terms.whyItMatters: Distance is the length of the path; different paths to the same place can give very different distances.
terms.whereItIs: The ribbon of course the hiker follow leaves.
